newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen-restructuring to generate higher turnover.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen-restructuring to generate higher turnover.

text.p: German engineering group Thyssen AG said on Monday that the group's restructuring plan would boost turnover, with sales of 45 billion marks ($27.5 billion) by the end of the century a realistic possibility.

Thyssen chief executive Dieter Vogel said at the group's annual news conference that he did not rule out a possible dip in sales in intervening years. In 1995/96, Thyssen sales were 38.7 billion marks.
Vogel said that the group had so far realised 2.8 billion marks in savings from the total of five billion marks in savings anticipated by the group.

Thyssen last November set a restructuring plan which foresaw focusing and growing its five core businesses of flat steel, elevator manufacturing, car parts, production systems and materials trading. ($ = 1.636 German Marks)
